chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Imran Al-Armani, from Abdullah ibn Al-Hakam, from Isa ibn Atiyya, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I had vowed not to drink from the milk of my goat, nor eat from its flesh, so I sold it, and with me are its children.' He said, 'Do not drink from their milk, nor eat from their flesh, for they are from her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming the offspring of an animal if one has vowed to abstain from the mother's milk and meat?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *tawallud* (offspring inheriting the status of the parent) within the context of *nadhr* (vows), specifically addressing whether the vow's restriction extends to the progeny. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that since the offspring is considered part of the mother's essence or property, the vow prohibiting consumption of the mother's milk and meat logically extends to her young, preventing the vow-maker from circumventing the oath by retaining the offspring. This ruling underscores the precision Shia jurisprudence applies to the linguistic and logical implications of personal vows.
